info.name: SockOdds API v1
info.description:
Bookmaker prices SockOdds records itself, readable identifiers, recorded price history and graded results for Australian and global sport.

Generated from openapi.json by scripts/generate_postman.py (contract version 1.0.0).

Set the `sockoddsKey` collection variable to your key, as the current value only, so it is never shared or exported. Get a free key at https://sockodds.com/signup/.

Ids, dates and keys in the example values are placeholders: replace them with values from your own responses.

query.description: Required. Who issued the id: `espn`, `afl` for AFLW match ids, or `nrl` for Rugby League World Cup match ids.
One official event id. Use this or `refs`, not both.
Comma-separated official event ids, at most 100. Use this or `ref`, not both.

request.description:
Find our event from an official event id: ESPN's event id, the AFL's match id (`CD_M` and digits) for AFLW, or the NRL's match id (digits) for the Rugby League World Cup. Send `ref` for one event, or `refs` for up to 100 at once. With `ref`, the response is the event, or 404 when no event carries that id. With `refs`, the response lists the ids that matched, in the order sent, each with its event; ids that match nothing are left out. A merged event returns the event it was merged into. Only official sources can be looked up, never a bookmaker's listing id. Free: costs no credits.

Reference: https://sockodds.com/docs/#lookupEvents
Reference: https://sockodds.com/docs/#getEvent

item.name: Prices

query.description: How prices are grouped. `market` (the default) lists each market and outcome once, with every bookmaker's price under the outcome in `prices`, best price first. `bookmaker` lists each bookmaker with its own copy of the markets, the shape v1 launched with.

Comma-separated non-participation rules (`void`, `loses`, `under`, `fair_price`). Keeps only player-market prices whose bookmaker settles a player who takes no part by one of these rules; prices on every other market are unaffected. For example `non_participant=void` keeps only player prices that are refunded when the player does not play.

Pro and Business only. Adds `opening`, `closing` or both, as requested, to each price, from that bookmaker's own quotes observed strictly before a cutoff (a quote stamped exactly at the cutoff does not count). For every sport but MMA the cutoff is the event's `scheduled_start`, so in-play quotes never count. For an MMA bout, whose `scheduled_start` is its card segment's start, the cutoff once the bout has been observed live or final (first at F) is the last poll that still showed it `scheduled` before F, but never earlier than the earlier of `scheduled_start` and F; a bout never observed live or final uses `scheduled_start`.

request.description:
Current prices for one event, grouped by market: each market and outcome appears once, and each outcome lists every bookmaker's price in `prices`, best price first. Markets come in catalogue order, then period, subject and line; outcomes in the market's side order. Use `group_by=bookmaker` for one block per bookmaker instead (the shape v1 launched with). Costs the unique markets returned x regions, in credits. See Plans and limits.

Reference: https://sockodds.com/docs/#getEventOdds

query.description: UTC date and time. With neither starts_after nor starts_before, the list starts 48 hours ago (live and upcoming games plus the last two days), and international cricket Tests (league cricket) are listed for six days from their start; name a window to list older games.
UTC date and time. Give starts_after, starts_before or both to list games outside the default window (from 48 hours ago; six days for cricket Tests).

How prices are grouped. `market` (the default) lists each market and outcome once, with every bookmaker's price under the outcome in `prices`, best price first. `bookmaker` lists each bookmaker with its own copy of the markets, the shape v1 launched with.

Comma-separated non-participation rules (`void`, `loses`, `under`, `fair_price`). Keeps only player-market prices whose bookmaker settles a player who takes no part by one of these rules; prices on every other market are unaffected. For example `non_participant=void` keeps only player prices that are refunded when the player does not play.

request.description:
Current prices for a page of events (25 by default, up to 100), grouped by market as on /events/{event_id}/odds unless `group_by=bookmaker`. Pages follow events; a cursor works only with the filters and grouping it was issued for, so follow `links.next`. Filters apply to prices before grouping: an outcome or market with no matching price is left out, and an event with none has an empty `markets` list. Costs credits: featured markets x regions once per page of up to 25 events, other markets per event. See Plans and limits.

Reference: https://sockodds.com/docs/#listOdds

Paid plans only. Own observations recorded under the new identities only. No observation predates 22 December 2025 UTC. Changes older than the live store keeps are read from the daily history archive and returned in the same shape and order, so a window reads the same whichever store holds it. Changes are ordered by observation time, then by when they were recorded. A window may not exceed 24 hours. While older history is busy the API answers 503 with a short Retry-After.

Reference: https://sockodds.com/docs/#listOddsHistory

item.description: The odds stream is a WebSocket, so it is not in this collection: see https://sockodds.com/docs/streaming/.

query.description: Restrict results to one independent event identity.

request.description:
Settled outcomes for finished events, graded from official result sources. Each outcome's `verdict` is `won`, `lost`, `void` (stake returned), `dead_heat`, `half_won` or `half_lost`. `half_won` / `half_lost` settle an Asian quarter line (x.25 / x.75) whose two half stakes split: one half won (or lost) at the quoted price and the other half refunded. A dead heat pays `dead_heat_factor` of the stake at the quoted price and loses the rest: a drawn AFL or AFLW head-to-head, a drawn AFLW quarter or half winner, a tied NBL quarter or half winner, and a Rugby League World Cup head-to-head still level after golden point, is a dead heat with a factor of 0.5. Outcomes that official evidence cannot settle are left out, never guessed. Each market settles on its own once official evidence settles all of its outcomes, so a result can be published while other markets on the event are still pending: `settlement` is `partial` and `pending_markets` counts them, and later results for the same event add the newly settled outcomes without changing any verdict already published. Each result also carries `box_score`: the official statistics the result is graded from (score by period, event and team totals, the player statistics SockOdds grades by player ID, and any athletes the source lists that the player registry cannot identify), or null until they have been read.

Reference: https://sockodds.com/docs/#listResults

Paid plans only. Whole days of history as Parquet files, one file per league and UTC day, from 22 December 2025 up to two days ago. Each file holds the rows /v1/odds/history returns for that league and day, sorted by event and observation time. Own observations only. Listing costs 1 credit.

Reference: https://sockodds.com/docs/#listHistoryFiles

Paid plans only. Downloads one day of history as a zstd Parquet file. Columns: event_id, market_id, market_key, market_name, period, subject_key, subject_id, subject_name, outcome_id, outcome_name, side, line, bookmaker, observed_at (UTC, milliseconds), kind, decimal_odds, implied_probability. The ETag is the file's SHA-256. At most two downloads at a time per key. Each download costs 100 credits. A file that names a player whose identity came under review after it was built answers 503 until it is rebuilt overnight.

Reference: https://sockodds.com/docs/#getHistoryFile

item.name: Racing

query.description: UTC date and time. Defaults to 6 hours ago.
UTC date and time. Defaults to 48 hours after starts_after. At most 8 days after starts_after.

request.description:
Australian and New Zealand races: thoroughbred, harness and greyhound. Paid plans (and the Pro trial); Developer keys get 403. Races come in start order, 25 a page by default, up to 100. With neither starts_after nor starts_before the list runs from 6 hours ago to 48 hours ahead; a window may span at most 8 days. Free: costs no credits. Race ids are SockOdds racing ids such as `thoroughbred_2026-11-17_AUS_scone_r1` (code, date, country, meeting, race number), not the `ev_` ids sport uses.

Reference: https://sockodds.com/docs/#listRaces

One race with its field: each runner's number (saddlecloth, or box for greyhounds), name, barrier, jockey (the driver in harness; null for greyhounds), trainer, weight, claim, form figures, silk colours and whether it is scratched or an emergency; and the race's class and conditions, prize money, track condition, weather, rail position and places paid, as stated on the TAB race page (null until that page has been read). `result` carries the placings by runner number and the scratched numbers once the race is resulted, else null; the full result with dividends is at `/racing/races/{race_id}/result`. Free: costs no credits.

Reference: https://sockodds.com/docs/#getRace

query.description: Pro and Business only. Adds `opening` (the first price recorded for the runner, and the bookmaker that offered it) and `closing` (the last price before the jump, and the bookmaker; with the Betfair Exchange back and lay at the jump) per runner, for win and place. `closing` is null until the race has jumped.

request.description:
Current fixed-odds win and place prices for every runner, one entry per bookmaker, and Betfair Exchange back and lay prices with the size available and the volume matched (AUD). `available` is true while the race has not jumped and the price was observed in the last 600 seconds. Scratched runners carry no prices. Costs 1 credit per region, 5 with opening and closing prices. See Plans and limits.

Reference: https://sockodds.com/docs/#getRaceOdds

Paid plans only. Every recorded change of a win or place price for one race, by runner and bookmaker, in observation order. A window may span at most 24 hours; racing movement is recorded from 16 November 2026 23:09 UTC. At most `limit` changes are returned; `meta.truncated` is true when the window may hold more, so ask again from the last `observed_at`.

Reference: https://sockodds.com/docs/#listRaceHistory

query.description: UTC date and time. Defaults to 6 hours ago.
UTC date and time. At most 8 days after starts_after.

request.description:
Race meetings: one racing code at one track on one day, each with its races in start order and the track condition, weather and rail position last stated for it. Same plans, filters and window as the races list (6 hours ago to 48 hours ahead by default, at most 8 days). A meeting id is its races' id without the race number, such as `thoroughbred_2026-11-17_AUS_scone`. Free: costs no credits.

Reference: https://sockodds.com/docs/#listMeetings

query.description: UTC date and time. Defaults to 24 hours ago.
UTC date and time. Defaults to now. At most 8 days after starts_after.

request.description:
Resulted races in start order, each with its placings (runner number, position, name, and the TAB fixed and tote prices the placegetters paid), scratchings with their deductions, tote pool totals and tote dividends (win, place, quinella, exacta, trifecta, first four and the multi-race pools TAB declared). With no window the list covers the last 24 hours; a window may span at most 8 days. Results exist from 1 August 2026; dividends and prices paid come with them where the TAB result page was recorded. Costs 2 credits a call.

Reference: https://sockodds.com/docs/#listRaceResults

The full result of one race: placings with the prices paid (TAB fixed win and place, tote win and place, and Betfair Starting Price), scratchings with deductions, tote pools and dividends, and `betfair_sp`: the Betfair Starting Price of every runner for win and place with the pre-play and in-play traded range and volume (AUD), from Betfair's published BSP files (Australian races; they arrive the day after the race). `result` is null until the race is resulted. Positions are the placegetters' (first four). Costs 1 credit a call.

Reference: https://sockodds.com/docs/#getRaceResult

TAB tote pools for one race: the total in each pool (AUD), each runner's tote win and place dividend, and, once the race is resulted, the declared dividends by pool. `stage` is `approximate` while betting is open (the dividends move with the pool until it closes) and `final` after the result; null when the pools have not been read yet. Read about every 20 minutes in the three hours before a race and every minute in the last 15. Costs 1 credit a call.

Reference: https://sockodds.com/docs/#getRaceTote

query.description: UTC date and time within the next 24 hours. Defaults to 3 hours ahead.
Smallest move to list, as a fraction of the opening price.

request.description:
Pro and Business only. Market movers across races still to run: for each runner the opening win price (the first price any bookmaker showed, and who) against the median and the best current fixed-odds win price, largest move first. `change` is (median now - opening) / opening: negative is firming, positive is drifting. Only prices observed in the last 600 seconds count, Betfair Exchange is not part of the median, and a runner whose opening price came from a bookmaker outside your request is left out. Looks at races from now to `starts_before` (3 hours ahead by default, 24 at most). Answers are reused for 20 seconds. Costs 10 credits a call.

Reference: https://sockodds.com/docs/#listRaceMovers

query.description: UTC date and time within the next 24 hours. Defaults to 3 hours ahead.

request.description:
Pro and Business only. Racing arbs on the win market in races still to run: the best fixed-odds win price at a bookmaker against the Betfair Exchange win lay price, where backing at the bookmaker and laying on the exchange returns a profit whichever way the race goes. `margin` = back x (1 - commission) / (lay - commission) - 1, the profit per unit staked on the back bet; `lay_stake_per_unit` = back / (lay - commission). `commission` is the exchange commission you pay (0.05 unless you pass yours; `meta.commission` echoes it). Both prices were observed in the last 600 seconds; `lay.size` is the AUD available at the lay price, so check it covers your lay stake, and check both prices before betting. Place markets are not compared (place terms differ between a bookmaker and the exchange). Looks at races from now to `starts_before` (3 hours ahead by default, 24 at most). Answers are reused for 20 seconds. Costs 10 credits a call.

Reference: https://sockodds.com/docs/#listRaceArbs

Form for every runner of a race: `form_figures` (the last-starts figures shown on the TAB race page, newest last) and `starts`, the runner's last starts before this race that SockOdds recorded, newest first: date, meeting, distance, class, track condition, jockey, trainer, barrier, weight, finishing position, field size and the prices it started at (TAB fixed, tote, Betfair SP). Recorded starts begin on 1 August 2026 (`meta.recorded_from`), so a runner's earlier career is not listed. `position` is 1 to 4 for a placegetter and null for a runner that finished further back. Runners are matched by name within a racing code. Costs 1 credit a call.

Reference: https://sockodds.com/docs/#getRaceForm

One runner's recorded starts, newest first, by racing code and name (case, punctuation and a country suffix such as (NZ) are ignored). The same fields as a race's form. Recorded starts begin on 1 August 2026. Costs 1 credit a call.

Reference: https://sockodds.com/docs/#getRunnerForm

Strike rates for each runner's jockey (the driver in harness), trainer and the jockey and trainer together, over the `days` before the race: starts, wins, seconds, thirds, `win_rate` (wins / starts) and `place_rate` (first three / starts). Counted only from races SockOdds recorded (from 1 August 2026) in the same racing code, so they are rates over that record, not career figures. Greyhounds have a trainer only. Costs 1 credit a call.

Reference: https://sockodds.com/docs/#getRaceConnections

Strike rates for one jockey (or driver), one trainer, or the two together, by name within a racing code, over the last `days` days of recorded races: starts, wins, seconds, thirds, win and place rate, and the first and last recorded start. Give `jockey`, `trainer` or both. Costs 1 credit a call.

Reference: https://sockodds.com/docs/#getConnectionStats

item.description: Australian and New Zealand thoroughbred, harness and greyhound racing: meetings and fields, fixed-odds and exchange prices, tote pools and dividends, results, Betfair Starting Price, movement, movers, arbs, form and strike rates.

item.name: Opportunities

query.description: Lowest profit to list, in percent of the total stake.
Oldest price to use, in seconds since it was observed. An entry is listed only while every price in it is at most this old.

request.description:
Pro and above. Arbitrage: two prices at two different bookmakers that cover both sides of one market, so backing both in the listed proportions returns a profit whichever side wins. Upcoming events only, best profit first, 25 a page by default, up to 100. The list is recomputed about every four minutes from the prices SockOdds records; each entry carries the time each price was observed, when the entry was computed and when it expires. By default an entry is listed only while both prices were observed in the last 600 seconds (`max_age`). Only bookmakers your key may read are used. Costs 10 credits a call; an empty answer costs nothing. Prices move: check the price at the bookmaker before acting on any entry.

Reference: https://sockodds.com/docs/#listArbitrage

query.description: Highest combined margin to list, in percent.
Oldest price to use, in seconds since it was observed. An entry is listed only while every price in it is at most this old.

request.description:
Pro and above. Low holds: the best price on each side of one market at two different bookmakers, where the two together carry almost no margin. `hold_pct` is that combined margin in percent (0 is break-even). Lowest hold first. Filters, paging, freshness and metering are as for arbitrage; `bookmakers` keeps the entries whose two prices are both at the named bookmakers.

Reference: https://sockodds.com/docs/#listLowHolds

query.description: Lowest middle profit to list, in percent of the total stake.
Oldest price to use, in seconds since it was observed. An entry is listed only while every price in it is at most this old.

request.description:
Pro and above. Middles: two bets on different lines of one market at two bookmakers (over 44.5 at one, under 47.5 at the other), so both win when the result lands in the gap. `gap` is the distance between the lines, `middle_profit_pct` the profit in percent of the total stake when both win, and `profit_pct` the result when only one wins (negative unless the pair is also an arbitrage). Largest middle profit first. `min_edge` is the lowest `middle_profit_pct` to list. Filters, paging, freshness and metering are as for arbitrage.

Reference: https://sockodds.com/docs/#listMiddles

query.description: Lowest expected value to list, in percent.
Oldest price to use, in seconds since it was observed. An entry is listed only while every price in it is at most this old.

request.description:
Pro and above. Positive expected value: a bookmaker price longer than the fair price of the outcome. `fair` says how the fair price was made: `sharp_book` (one sharp bookmaker's two-sided market with its margin removed, named in `fair.bookmaker`), `exchange` (an exchange's back and lay prices) or `consensus` (the margin-free prices of `fair.books` other bookmakers, combined; never the bookmaker being priced). `ev_pct` is the expected profit in percent of the stake and `kelly_pct` the full-Kelly stake in percent of bankroll. Highest `ev_pct` first. Upcoming events only; freshness, paging and metering are as for arbitrage. An estimate, not a guarantee: a fair price is a model of the market, and prices move.

Reference: https://sockodds.com/docs/#listPositiveEv

item.description: Arbitrage, low holds, middles and positive expected value, computed from the prices SockOdds records. Pro and above.

item.name: Analysis

query.description: How the margin is removed. `proportional` (the default) divides each implied probability by their sum. `power` raises each to the one exponent that makes them sum to 1, which takes more margin off long prices.

request.description:
Pro and above. Fair prices for a league's events: each market's prices with the bookmaker margin removed. The base is Pinnacle's own two-sided (or three-way) market when Pinnacle prices every outcome of it (`fair.source` `sharp_book`); otherwise the median of every bookmaker that prices the whole market, each with its own margin removed, when at least three do (`consensus`). A market with neither base is left out, as are markets whose runners are players or scores. Each outcome carries its fair probability and fair decimal odds, and `best_price`: the best current price among the bookmakers your key may read, with its edge against the fair price. With no start window the list holds events that started at most 12 hours ago and upcoming ones, in start order, 25 a page at most. Main lines only unless `alternates=true`. Costs 5 credits a call; an empty answer costs nothing.

Reference: https://sockodds.com/docs/#listFairOdds

query.description: How the margin is removed. `proportional` (the default) divides each implied probability by their sum. `power` raises each to the one exponent that makes them sum to 1, which takes more margin off long prices.

request.description:
Pro and above. Fair prices for one event, as `/fair-odds` describes them. `bookmakers` limits both the bookmakers a consensus is built from and the bookmakers `best_price` is chosen among.

Reference: https://sockodds.com/docs/#getEventFairOdds

query.description: How the margin is removed. `proportional` (the default) divides each implied probability by their sum. `power` raises each to the one exponent that makes them sum to 1, which takes more margin off long prices.
The outcome you bet on. Give it with `odds`.
The decimal odds you took. Give it with `outcome_id`.

request.description:
Pro and above. The closing line of one event: each bookmaker's opening and closing price per outcome (as `snapshots=opening,closing` returns them), the fair closing price per outcome (`closing_fair`, built from the closing prices as `/fair-odds` builds a fair price) and `opening_clv_pct`, the closing line value of each bookmaker's opening price: how far that price beat the fair closing price, in percent (positive beat the close). Give `outcome_id` and `odds` together to get the closing line value of your own bet in `bet`. Without `markets` the main markets are read (winner, result, handicap and the game totals); name up to 20 market keys for others. Closing prices are null until the event has started. Costs 10 credits a call.

Reference: https://sockodds.com/docs/#getEventClosing

query.description: Minutes to look back, in steps of 5.
Fewest bookmakers that moved the same way.

request.description:
Pro and above. Line moves in one league: markets whose main line (handicap, totals, player and team over/unders) changed at one or more bookmakers in the last `window` minutes, upcoming events only. Each bookmaker counts once, by its net move in the window (a line that moved and came back is not a move). `steam` is true when at least `min_books` bookmakers moved the same way and they are at least two thirds of the bookmakers that moved; `sharp` is true when Pinnacle is among them. `from_line` and `to_line` are the median line of those bookmakers before and after; for a handicap the line is the home side's (competitor 1 in tennis). Steam first, then the most bookmakers. Lines are sampled every few minutes, so a move is timed to the sample that first saw it. Markets with no line (head to head) are not covered. Costs 10 credits a call; an empty answer costs nothing.

Reference: https://sockodds.com/docs/#listLineMoves

item.description: Prices with the bookmaker margin removed, closing prices and closing line value, and line moves across bookmakers. Pro and above.
